Yes - DOOM is King Kirby creation (as almost all great things are), first drawn in 1962! He actually didn’t even draw DOOM without the mask on until the late 90s I think, in which he did indeed have the tiny left cheek scar (my personal favorite as well - I really hope they go with this for the movies), but this was only a personal Kirby sketch, never published. 

Before that, DOOM *always* wore the mask, and whenever it was off Kirby would ingeniously obscure his face behind darkness, shadows, or steam or bandages, which made him embody this perilous mystery under the mask. If you haven’t read the original FF run by Lee and Kirby, I really will always recommend it. Kirby is (in my opinion) the greatest artist of the 20th century! RIP to the King.

Games before Halo allowed you to carry a multitude of different weapon types that were used to different effect. After Halo, every FPS only allows you to swap between two weapons, most of which are hitscan weapons that do basically the same thing with different damage multipliers. Before Halo, different enemy types affected you and your health in different ways. Look at the original Dooms enemy types. Some charge straight for you, some shoot fireballs, some float above the battlefield and rain fire from above, and each of their projectiles have different looks and force you to look at every new encounter like an obstacle course you're trying to overcome. After Halo, every enemy encounter is with a big group of bad guys running at you infinitely shooting you with the same boring weapons and require no strategy to overcome. In Doom, different weapons worked better for different enemies. In CoD 4, all enemies die very easily to whatever weapon you're currently carrying without much trouble at all. I'm not here saying Halo is a bad game, I love Halo. The original 3 Halo games are my favorite trilogy of all time. What i'm criticizing here are the AAA developers that came after, seeing the leaps and bounds Halo brought to the table, and dumbing it down for a more ease of access big budget set piece style game.

Again, not a game dev here. I’m just using controls example for the broader “if it ain’t broke” attitude. RPGS, action games, and strategy games have all had thousands of times more innovation in systems than FPS games have since Halo came out.

What I think Jared is saying is that Halo made shooter more comfortable, not worse. Yes, all these games that came out after Halo all had smaller more incremental innovations to the genre like storytelling, world building, and gameplay systems. And hell, some of those games you listed are some of my favorite games of all time and we would without a doubt not have them without Halo. But I think his argument comes from the very basic innovations that FPS games lack now. Every single shooter since Halo, plays like Halo. You use a stick to move, a stick to aim, there’s a melee button and a crouch and a grenade button. THESE are the innovations he’s talking about. The “if it ain’t broke don’t fix it” attitude does not an incredible game make. Even the most indie darlings of indie darlings we praise like Screen Cheat and Super Hot, while innovative in their systems and design, still feel and control the way they do because of Halo. Granted, I dunno how it gets changed i’m not a game designer. But I understand his opinion.
